incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Binance systems/infrastructure to drain customer and platform cryptocurrency wallets in what the industry is calling the largest crypto heist on record.
incidents.impact: An estimated $5.5-6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen; roughly $1.8-3 billion was frozen by Tether and Circle, with the remainder escaping attacker control. Binance says user funds remain safe; the incident has reignited regulatory debate over digital-asset security.

incidents.victim: 200+ government, defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and telecom organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: A China-nexus actor ("Vapor Panda") used the agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX, paired with the DeepSeek LLM, to run automated, parallel intrusions issuing commands as often as every 10 seconds against foreign ministries, defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and telecom targets in at least 14 countries.
incidents.impact: Since Oct. 17, roughly 140 of 200+ targeted organizations were compromised or showed evidence of intrusion, including a European country's presidency and prime minister's office; the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor was deployed at several victims. CrowdStrike calls it the first nation-state agentic campaign at this scale.

incidents.victim: Belarus-Russia cyber campaign — Ukrainian transportation-sector manufacturer
incidents.vector: The Belarusian state-aligned group tracked as FrostyNeighbor (aka GhostWriter) deployed Chisel, UltraVNC, Cobalt Strike and a VBScript wiper via Group Policy against the victim's network.
incidents.impact: ESET documented the first publicly known destructive, data-wiping attack by a Belarus-aligned actor, signaling deeper operational alignment with Russia's cyber campaign against Ukraine; Belarus becomes only the sixth state publicly linked to wiper deployment.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education (Student Financial Aid website)
incidents.vector: An unauthorized party gained access to a system or database behind the Florida Student Financial Aid website.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, phone numbers, Social Security numbers and dates of birth of approximately 4.9 million financial-aid applicants were exposed; the site was taken offline. Financial aid disbursements are not affected.

incidents.victim: GMO Internet Group (Onamae Desktop Cloud / FX trading service)
incidents.vector: Hackers gained unauthorized access to GMO's Onamae Desktop Cloud service, which hosts the company's FX foreign-exchange trading platform.
incidents.impact: Attackers demanded a $50 million ransom and leaked some stolen data on the dark web this week; GMO is offering a $1 million reward for information identifying the hackers.

incidents.victim: U.S. government-affiliated network (via compromised Palo Alto Networks firewalls)
incidents.vector: Attackers chained the PHP2Shell PHP remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618/109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit against internet-facing Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management interfaces to obtain root access.
incidents.impact: Of roughly 240 targeted firewalls, 24 were compromised; two servers in a U.S. government-affiliated environment were deeply penetrated, yielding persistent access, Active Directory data, credentials and network topology. Palo Alto Networks confirmed the findings and had already patched the exploited PAN-OS flaw.

incidents.vector: An attacker compromised the Cursor Marketplace and replaced the legitimate Anthropic Claude Code extension with a trojanized version (2.1.313/2.1.312) containing a hidden loader, live for about 11 hours.
incidents.impact: The malicious loader attempted to install an SSH backdoor and reverse tunnel and exfiltrated host reconnaissance data from up to 5,000 installs; Cursor says admin-privilege requirements blocked actual SSH access on most hosts. Anthropic's own systems and the official npm/VS Code Marketplace packages were unaffected.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS/ICE/CBP employees)
incidents.vector: A hacktivist group calling itself "Department of Peace" breached an Okta single sign-on database used by DHS and published the data via a searchable archive called Icepick.
incidents.impact: Personal information on more than 41,000 DHS employees, mostly ICE and CBP personnel, dating back to 2011, was exposed; a takedown request from a DHS contractor only briefly disrupted access before the archive resurfaced under a new registrar.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised website-performance vendor DebugBear and injected wallet-draining JavaScript into its embed code, which ran on Polymarket's site.
incidents.impact: Trading was briefly halted after the compromise; an account allegedly siphoned more than $2.1 million in cryptocurrency from users. Polymarket says it will fully reimburse affected traders.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached Coinbase's third-party analytics provider, Amplitude.
incidents.impact: Some Coinbase customer data was stolen as a result of the upstream Amplitude compromise, according to Coinbase.

incidents.victim: Western media, NGOs, and U.S. government/military entities (historic 2011-2014 campaign)
incidents.vector: Syrian Electronic Army operative Ahmad Umar Agha ("Th3Pr0") hacked roughly 47 Western media, business, NGO and government targets on behalf of the former Assad regime's intelligence service, including hijacking a news agency's Twitter account.
incidents.impact: A false 2013 tweet claiming an attack on the White House triggered a temporary $136 billion flash crash in the Dow Jones Industrial Average; after more than a decade as a fugitive, Agha was sentenced to 42 months in federal prison.

incidents.victim: Virtualine bulletproof hosting infrastructure (used by ransomware/cybercrime ecosystem)
incidents.vector: The DOJ and FBI obtained a court order to seize the primary domain of Virtualine, a Russian-speaking bulletproof hosting provider used by ransomware groups, infostealer operators and CSAM distributors.
incidents.impact: Virtualine had facilitated ransomware (including Coinbase Cartel, The Gentlemen, INC, DragonForce and Qilin), sextortion, money laundering and malware distribution; researchers note the takedown disrupted but did not fully dismantle the operation.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the FEC's electronic filing system, which tracks political party campaign spending.
incidents.impact: The agency shut down its electronic filing system a week before the midterm elections as a precaution; the FEC says the outage has no impact on the voting process itself.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center (hospitals, medical school)
incidents.vector: A ransomware gang calling itself "BYOD" encrypted hospital and medical-school systems.
incidents.impact: The attack forced ambulance diversions, cancelled dozens of outpatient surgeries and appointments, and disrupted classes; UNM did not pay a ransom and restored all facilities by Oct. 28. The attackers claim to retain stolen patient and employee data and are attempting to extort individuals directly.

incidents.victim: Zenith Technology (New Zealand clinical trial/lab services provider)
incidents.vector: The Zawoo ransomware group compromised Zenith Technology, a provider of clinical trial and analytical laboratory services, at the start of September 2026.
incidents.impact: The attack delayed lab work for New Zealand patients and has also delayed coronial autopsy investigations across the country.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Moldovan government networks and began extracting data; IT staff detected the exfiltration in progress.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly one-third of Moldova's population was stolen; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime and shipping companies
incidents.vector: The ransomware/extortion group "n0n" compromised maritime IT services provider CyberLogitec and pivoted from its network into the environments of downstream customers.
incidents.impact: More than 40 port authorities and shipping companies were listed on n0n's leak site after payment deadlines expired; roughly half of the victims are known CyberLogitec customers.

incidents.vector: An attacker compromised more than 330 Tor relays with the Ebury Linux malware, converting them into malicious exit nodes.
incidents.impact: The attacker intercepted SSH connections and downgraded email connections to steal unencrypted traffic for three days before a Swiss engineer detected and reported the campaign; compromised relays represented roughly 10% of Tor exit capacity.
